title: West African talking drums can imitate human speech
body: Many West African languages, such as Yoruba, are tonal: the pitch of a syllable changes its meaning. The hourglass-shaped talking drum, called dùndún in Yoruba, has cords a player squeezes under the arm to raise or lower its pitch, copying the tones and rhythms of spoken phrases. Skilled drummers can recite proverbs and praise poetry that knowing listeners understand, and drums were used to send messages over long distances.

steps.label: Yoruba: a syllable’s pitch changes meaning

The beats copy the phrase’s tones and rhythm
Listeners who know the phrase understand it
